blocks.text: I can ask and answer intonation questions to identify something.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Pronounced ‘ch’ as in ‘chercher’, which means ‘to look for’.
The rise and fall of the voice in speaking.

blocks.text: The sound [ch] sounds like the ‘ch’ in ‘chercher’, which means ‘to look for’. Listen, repeat and read these words.
Read these words with [ch]. Say them aloud.

blocks.label: Why can’t you hear the ‘t’ in chocolat?
blocks.text: The ‘t’ at the end of chocolat is a silent final consonant, so you do not say it.
To change a statement into an intonation question, you raise your voice at the end.
These are also called yes/no questions because the answer is always yes or no.
You can also ask a question with ‘ou’, which means ‘or’.

items: C’est une peluche ou c’est un animal ?

blocks.text: Un animal means ‘an animal’, so this answer says it is an animal.

blocks.q: You say ‘C’est une banane’ and raise your voice at the end. What have you made?
blocks.why: Raising your voice at the end of a statement makes an intonation question, which is a yes/no question.

blocks.q: Is this a yes/no question? ‘C’est un stylo ?’
options: Yes, the answer is yes or no
No, the answer is a number
blocks.why: The answer to a yes/no question is always yes or no.

blocks.text: You can also use intonation to ask an information question, for example ‘what?’. You put a question word after ‘c’est’.
‘Quoi’ means ‘what’ in French, and ‘c’est quoi ?’ means ‘what is it?’. In English it is different: we usually put question words at the start.

blocks.q: Match the French to the English.
Someone asks ‘C’est quoi ?’ Choose the correct answer.

blocks.text: When learning a new language it is important to practise vocabulary regularly to strengthen your memory.

items: The words you learnt most recently are the easiest to remember.
The words learnt a month ago need a bit more effort.
Words learnt before that need hard work.

blocks.label: Why practise?
blocks.text: Practising helps you remember words you learnt recently, know how to spell, pronounce and recognise them, and make them stick in your long-term memory. It is like a vocabulary workout: the more you train your brain, the easier it is to remember new words.

blocks.q: Match the French word to the English.
How often should you practise new vocabulary?
blocks.why: New words have to be practised regularly or you might forget them.

items: The sound [ch] sounds like the ‘ch’ in ‘chercher’, which means ‘to look for’.
You make an intonation question by raising your voice at the end of a statement: c’est un chat ?
You can make an information question by adding a question word after c’est, like ‘quoi’, which means ‘what’: c’est quoi ?
Practise vocabulary regularly to strengthen your memory.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: What is it? Intonation questions and ‘quoi’
worksheet.instructions: Answer with one word or a short phrase. In the un/une questions, choose un for a masculine noun and une for a feminine noun.

questions.prompt: What does the French word ‘quoi’ mean in English?
What does ‘c’est quoi ?’ mean in English?
questions.explanation: C’est means ‘it is’ and quoi means ‘what’, so c’est quoi ? means ‘What is it?’.

questions.prompt: To change ‘C’est un chat.’ into a question, you raise your ___ at the end. Which word fills the gap?
questions.explanation: An intonation question is made by raising your voice at the end of a statement.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the rise and fall of the voice in speaking?
questions.explanation: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice in speaking.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with un or une: C’est ___ chat.
questions.explanation: Chat is masculine, so we use un.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with un or une: C’est ___ photo.
questions.explanation: Photo is feminine, so we use une.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with un or une: C’est ___ animal.
questions.explanation: Animal is masculine, so we use un.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with un or une: C’est ___ bouteille.
questions.explanation: Bouteille is feminine, so we use une.
